chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about a man who sent his dog (for hunting), and when he reached the game, it had already killed it
He said: 'Eat, even if it (the dog) has eaten (from it).'

key_terms.أَرْسَلَ: sent/released — the technical term for dispatching a trained hunting animal, a key condition for lawful hunting
key_terms.أَكَلَ: it ate — refers to the dog eating from the prey before the hunter retrieved it
key_terms.كَلْب: hunting dog (kalb) — in Islamic jurisprudence, specifically refers to a trained hunting dog (al-kalb al-mu'allam) whose prey is permissible to eat
key_terms.كُلْ: eat — the imperative form, indicating a legal ruling permitting consumption

ai.seo_question: Is game hunted by a dog permissible to eat if the dog ate part of the prey in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Yunus ibn Ya'qub reports asking Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether game hunted by a trained dog is permissible to eat even if the dog consumed part of the prey before the hunter arrived. The Imam ruled that it is permissible to eat, even in this circumstance. This hadith addresses a practical concern in Islamic hunting law (sayd), establishing that partial consumption by the hunting dog does not invalidate the permissibility (halal status) of the remaining prey.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhassan Bin Ahmad, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said, 
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
about a man who sent his dog (for hunting). So when he came to it, and it had killed it’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat, and even if it has eaten (from it)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhsin ibn Ahmad from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the case of a man who sends his dog and he arrives at the site when the dog has killed the prey.
He (the Imam) said, ‘You can use it for food even if the dog has eaten thereof.’”
